heading: Suggestions, not errors
body:
Some code does its job, but a reader needs a moment to see what it does. `if (total > limit) { return true; } return false;` only returns the result of the comparison, so `return total > limit;` says the same thing more plainly. Tachyon knows a short list of these patterns. Each one is easier to read for a reader who learns English as a second language, and none of them is only shorter. A long line with many parts is not simpler: when code is hard to read because it does several things, move a part into a named private method instead (see Cohesive services).

`ty build`, `ty preview` and `ty test` print a suggestion for each pattern that they find. A suggestion is not an error: the command goes on and the app builds. Each suggestion names the file and the line, and its `help:` line shows the code in its simpler form:

```text
suggestion[TY1340]: This `if` only returns true or false. Return the condition itself.
  --> server/services/CartService.js:14
  help: return total > limit;
```

`ty migrate fix` lists every suggested change, and `ty migrate fix --write` applies them. A simpler form never changes what the code does. When a rewrite could change the result, Tachyon does not suggest it. For example, in JavaScript, Python and Ruby `if (user) { return true; } return false;` returns `true` or `false`, but `return user;` would return the user, so this pattern is suggested only when the condition is already a comparison or another true-or-false value.

Suggestions are on for both sides of the app. To hide them for Tac code, set `tac.simplify.suggest` to `false` in `client/manifest.json`. For Yon code, set `simplify.suggest` to `false` in `server/application.json`.
